introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Computer Science (0595), Paper 3 (practical), June 2024. Duration: two and a half hours. Do all the tasks (Task I, Task II and Task III) specified in this question paper.**

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All written answers should be provided in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Calculators are NOT allowed.

The booklet reproduced here contains three versions of the same practical paper, headed Group One (booklet 0000/0595/3/Grp 1), Group Three (Grp 3) and Group Four (Grp 4); a candidate sits only ONE group. Group One: Task I (word processing, 15 marks), Task II (spreadsheet, 20 marks), Task III (HTML, 15 marks). Group Three: Task 1 (word processing, 20 marks), Task 2 (spreadsheet, 15 marks), Task 3 (HTML, 15 marks). Group Four: Task I (word processing, 20 marks), Task II (spreadsheet, 20 marks), Task III (C or Pascal program, 10 marks). Each group is worth 50 marks.

The working files named in the tasks (pictures, logo, signature) are supplied on the day; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.

questions.enonce_markdown:
a) Use an appropriate spreadsheet Software to enter the information in Table 1. *[3 marks]*

Data to key in (columns A to E, rows 3 to 15, and the title in row 2):

| A | B | C | D | E |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S/N | Product | Quantity in Kg Sold | Selling Price Per Kg | Cost Price Per Kg |
| 1 | Rice | 75 | 475 | 350 |
| 2 | Maize | 90 | 400 | 250 |
| 3 | Beans | 125 | 450 | 245 |
| 4 | Soya Beans | 100 | 500 | 375 |
| 5 | Yams | 250 | 750 | 500 |
| 6 | Egusi | 79 | 2000 | 1350 |
| 7 | Garri | 100 | 600 | 400 |
| 8 | Groundnut | 73 | 500 | 375 |
| 9 | Cocoyam | 150 | 250 | 135 |
| 10 | Cassava | 145 | 200 | 75 |
| 11 | Irish Potatoes | 276 | 225 | 100 |
| 12 | Sweet Potato | 85 | 100 | 35 |

The title "Weekly sales for Mami Buy and Sell" goes in row 2 and the headings Unit Profit Per Kg, Sales revenue, Cost of Goods and Gross Profit Per Product go in F3:I3; the label "Total" goes in B16.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Open a spreadsheet program (for example *Microsoft Excel* or *LibreOffice Calc*) and a new workbook.

1. Row 2: type the title **Weekly sales for Mami Buy and Sell** in A2 (it can be merged and centred over A2:I2, as in the table).
2. Row 3: the headings **S/N, Product, Quantity in Kg Sold, Selling Price Per Kg, Cost Price Per Kg, Unit Profit Per Kg, Sales revenue, Cost of Goods, Gross Profit Per Product** in A3 to I3.
3. Rows 4 to 15: the twelve products with their serial numbers, quantities, selling prices and cost prices, as **numbers** (no unit or currency sign in the cells, so that formulas can use them).
4. Cell **B16**: the word **Total**.
5. Check each figure against Table 1 (for example Egusi: 79, 2000, 1350).

Marking idea (3 marks, indicative): title and headings (1); the twelve products and serial numbers (1); the numeric data correct (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: b) Bold the First and second rows and set the font size of the first row to 14points. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select rows 1 and 2 (click the row numbers 1 and 2 on the left) and click **Bold** (Ctrl + B). Then select row 1 only and choose the font size **14** in the size box. (In Table 1, row 1 is empty and the title is in row 2: apply the instruction as printed; it is also sensible to make the title row 2 bold, which this does.)

Marking idea (1 mark): bold on the first two rows and 14 points on the first row.

questions.enonce_markdown:
c) For Rice enter formulas to compute: Unit Profit per Kg, Sales Revenue, Cost of Goods and Gross Profit per Product. *[2 marks]*

- Unit Profit per Kg is Selling Price per Kg minus Cost Price per Kg.
- Sales revenue is Selling Price per Kg multiplied by Quantity in Kg sold.
- Cost of Good is Cost Price per Kg multiplied by Quantity in Kg
- Gross Profit per Product is Sales revenue minus Cost of Good.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Rice is in row 4: quantity in **C4** (75 kg), selling price in **D4** (475), cost price in **E4** (350). Type, in this order:

| Cell | Formula | Meaning | Result for Rice |
|---|---|---|---|
| F4 | `=D4-E4` | Unit Profit per Kg = selling price - cost price | 475 - 350 = 125 |
| G4 | `=C4*D4` | Sales revenue = quantity x selling price | 75 x 475 = 35,625 |
| H4 | `=C4*E4` | Cost of Goods = quantity x cost price | 75 x 350 = 26,250 |
| I4 | `=G4-H4` | Gross Profit = sales revenue - cost of goods | 35,625 - 26,250 = 9,375 |

Check: the gross profit is also the unit profit multiplied by the quantity: 125 x 75 = 9,375. Each formula starts with the sign =.

Marking idea (2 marks): the four formulas correct (0.5 each).

questions.enonce_markdown:
e) In the space below, write the formulas you have in cells F14 to I14. *[2 marks]*

F14 ____  G14 ____  H14 ____  I14 ____
questions.corrige_markdown:
Row 14 is the row of **Irish Potatoes** (quantity 276 in C14, selling price 225 in D14, cost price 100 in E14). The formulas of row 4 have been copied ten rows down, so every row number 4 became 14:

- **F14: `=D14-E14`** (225 - 100 = 125)
- **G14: `=C14*D14`** (276 x 225 = 62,100)
- **H14: `=C14*E14`** (276 x 100 = 27,600)
- **I14: `=G14-H14`** (62,100 - 27,600 = 34,500)

Marking idea (2 marks): 0.5 for each correct formula.

questions.enonce_markdown: f) Use the sum function in cell G15 to compute the total sales revenue. Copy the formula to cells H15 and I15. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **SUM** function adds a range of cells. The twelve products are in rows 4 to 15, so the range to add is **G4:G15**:

**`=SUM(G4:G15)`**

Copy this formula to the next two cells on its right (drag the fill handle to the right): H gives **`=SUM(H4:H15)`** and I gives **`=SUM(I4:I15)`**.

Results: total sales revenue **756,975**, total cost of goods **477,600**, total gross profit **279,375** (check: 756,975 - 477,600 = 279,375).

Note on the cell: the question names row 15, but in Table 1 row 15 is still the product Sweet Potato and the row labelled **Total** is **row 16**. The totals belong in the Total row (G16, H16, I16); typing a sum over G4:G15 into G15 itself would be a circular reference and would destroy the Sweet Potato value. The formula to give is the same in both readings.

Marking idea (2 marks): SUM with the correct range G4:G15 (1); copied to the two other columns (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: g) Write in the space below the formula you have in cell I15. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The formula in the total of the Gross Profit column is

**`=SUM(I4:I15)`**

(it is the total of column I, the copy of `=SUM(G4:G15)` moved two columns to the right; it is placed in the Total row, which is row 16 in Table 1, see the note of question f).

questions.enonce_markdown: h) Insert a pie chart that indicates the Goods Sold (Product) and their Quantities (Quantity in Kg sold) below your worksheet. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **pie chart** shows how a total is shared between categories (here the quantity sold of each product).

1. Select the product names **B4:B15**, then hold **Ctrl** and select the quantities **C4:C15** (a non-adjacent selection, so the headings and the other columns are left out).
2. Click **Insert > Chart > Pie** (a 2-D pie).
3. Add a title such as *Quantity in Kg sold per product*, show the legend (the product names) and, if possible, the data labels (quantities or percentages).
4. Drag the chart **below the worksheet** (from row 18 downwards), so that it does not cover the data.

The twelve slices share a total of 1548 kg; the three largest are Irish Potatoes 17.8 %, Yams 16.1 %, Cocoyam 9.7 %.

Marking idea (2 marks): a pie chart (1); built from the products and the quantities, with title or legend and placed below the worksheet (1).
